# Rift Awakening opposition

Use the named full stat blocks from the retained SRD 5.2.1 corpus in this Plan's Ruleset/reference snapshot. Animals are in content/corpus/animals.json; other creatures are in content/corpus/monsters.json. These are source paths within the Ruleset package, not Setting references. Apply their real attacks, traits, saves and damage types using the supported Ruleset operations; consult the retained source before constructing combat state. Cosmetic violet light grants no extra damage, teleportation or resistance.

The Plan places encounters by event and purpose. The GM determines ordinary surroundings from the location and current fiction, without compulsory tactical gimmicks. The intended starting party is a level-1 PC and at least one level-1 Companion. The campaign reaches 12 through its declared story milestones. Check the actual number and abilities of active participants before choosing the following rosters; levels alone do not establish difficulty.

## Profiles and roles

- Rift Wolves: SRD Wolf, animals page 364. These are affected local wolves, not the Setting's much stronger Rifthound shapechanger. One Wolf is the introductory baseline for a two-person level-1 party. They are hungry and frightened; driving them off or escaping can resolve the encounter.
- Root-touched vermin and woodland animals: Giant Rat, Boar, Black Bear and Wolf. Early animals keep their ordinary stat blocks. They defend food or young and can be distracted or driven away.
- Paid guards and pass robbers: Bandit and Scout; Bandit Captain (monsters page 261) is a leader from the middle of the campaign, not a default level-1 enemy. They value survival, wages and plausible amnesty.
- Raider hardliners: Berserker (page 263) or Bandit Captain. These are locally equipped humanoids without the separate Setting Rift Raider's plane-shift or psychic weapon powers.
- Hired champions: Gladiator (page 289), with ordinary Scouts or Bandits only when warranted. Do not send several champions against a small party merely because a scene is late in the story.
- Predators: Dire Wolf, Owlbear or Giant Crocodile, selected for actual habitat. A larger creature can be a single substantial opponent rather than a pack of identical high-damage enemies.
- Rift echoes: Specter (page 327) or Wraith (page 342). Use their actual undead mechanics and state which is present. Life-draining enemies are dangerous to small parties; prefer one Specter early and reserve Wraiths for the later Hollows. Do not invent instant death or irreversible memory theft.
- Lesser Warden constructs: Animated Armor (page 259). Shield Guardian (page 323) is substantially stronger and has a real controlling amulet; identify its current holder and adjudicate control as written.
- Major Warden custodian: Stone Golem (page 330), including the Vigilant Engine. An authenticated maintenance override is an authored noncombat resolution to its orders, not a universal mechanical weakness.
- Rift manifestations: Air, Earth or Fire Elemental as explicitly chosen. Their violet appearance is cosmetic; use the real elemental damage and abilities, not invented unresistible 'Rift damage'.

## Party scale

For PC plus one Companion, favor a single relevant foe or a small group of weaker creatures. Separate encounters with opportunities to assess danger and recover under the Ruleset. At levels 4–7 a Captain with one supporting Bandit is meaningfully different from a full raiding warband. At levels 8–11 one Wraith, Gladiator or appropriately telegraphed custodian can carry a scene. Do not combine every profile named in an act into one encounter.

For larger parties, add weaker supporting actors whose jobs make sense before increasing the number of powerful creatures. Retain room for retreat, surrender and alternate approaches. Use actual SRD encounter-building guidance, current HP/resources and character abilities; these are starting rosters, not a claim that all party compositions are balanced. Never secretly reduce statistics after initiative or restore resources between scenes.

For a two-person level-12 finale that cannot reasonably face the full Stone Golem, the authored damaged Vigilant Engine variant has 120 maximum HP and one Slam attack on its turn instead of Multiattack; every other statistic and ability is the retained Stone Golem's, including its actual Slow ability and immunities. Declare and record that variant before combat. A larger or stronger party may face the intact profile. No additional guardian is compulsory. If the intact profile remains unsuitable, competent coalition allies can participate under supported rules, or the authenticated override can be pursued; no optional side quest is required.

## Rewards and recovery

No creature's printed XP is awarded in this milestone campaign. The main story's levels apply to the whole active party using the Ruleset's advancement procedures. Record only actual treasure, payments and accepted gifts. The inn, refuge and camps can provide normal rest opportunities; use the Ruleset for their effects. Named magic consumables use actual admitted item definitions, not new effects invented by this guide.
